input: Fix the broken fence panel in the backyard

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the panel needs a full replacement or just structural repair (e.g., loose boards, broken pickets) determines the materials needed and the complexity of the work.
Whether this is a DIY job or requires hiring a contractor changes the entire plan — tools, budget, scheduling, and skill requirements all shift.
The fence material (wood, vinyl, metal, composite) dictates what replacement parts to source and what repair techniques apply.
A tight budget or deadline (e.g., an upcoming event, a landlord inspection) would force prioritisation of speed or cost-cutting approaches.
Knowing whether replacement parts are already on hand or need to be sourced determines the immediate next action — hardware store run vs. starting work now.
The desired end result — purely functional fix vs. aesthetically matched finish — affects whether a quick patch suffices or a full panel swap is needed.
Any constraints around who owns the fence (shared with a neighbour, rental property) could involve permissions or shared costs that change the approach.

gold.taskTitle: Fix broken fence panel in the backyard
gold.taskDescription: Repair or replace a damaged fence panel located in the backyard.

questions.title: Is the panel fully broken or partially damaged?
questions.description: Determine the extent of the damage — e.g., one snapped picket, a sagging panel, or a completely collapsed section — to scope the repair correctly.

questions.title: What material is the fence made from?
questions.description: Identify whether the fence is wood, vinyl, metal, composite, or another material, as this dictates repair methods and where to source parts.

questions.title: Will you do this yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is a DIY repair or a job to outsource to a handyman or fencing contractor.

questions.title: Do you already have tools and replacement materials?
questions.description: Establish whether a hardware store run is needed before work can begin, or if everything is already available on-site.

questions.title: Is there a deadline or urgency driving this repair?
questions.description: Find out if there is a time pressure — such as a neighbour complaint, landlord inspection, or upcoming garden event — that affects prioritisation.

questions.title: Does the repaired panel need to match the existing fence visually?
questions.description: Determine whether a purely functional fix is acceptable or whether the finish, colour, and style must match the rest of the fence.

questions.title: Is the fence shared with a neighbour or on a rental property?
questions.description: Check for any ownership, permission, or cost-sharing considerations that could affect how and when the repair is carried out.
